chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about wearing a ring in the right hand, and I said, 'I saw the Banu Hashim wearing rings in their right hands.' So he said: 'My father wore rings in his left, and he was superior to them and more knowledgeable.'
ai.seo_question: Is it preferred to wear a ring in the right or left hand according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the flexibility in wearing a ring, contrasting the general preference for the right hand with the specific practice of Imam Ali (peace be upon him), who wore his in the left. By citing his father as 'the most excellent and most knowledgeable' among the Banu Hashim, the Imam establishes that superior scholarly and spiritual status validates personal variations in ritual practice, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the Imams' authoritative interpretation of Sunnah.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about wearing the ring in the right hand, and I said, ‘I saw the Clan of Hashim wearing rings in their right hands’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> wore rings in his<sup>asws</sup> left, and he<sup>asws</sup> was higher than them, and of more understanding’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Yahya ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about wearing the ring on the right hand saying, ‘I have seen banu Hashim wearing rings on their right hands.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘My father would wear it on his left hand and he was the most excellent among them with more power of wisdom.’” (This is because of Taqiyah, according to al-Majlisy)
